To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Oxoid VET RPLA test was the most reliable method for detection of heat-stable enterotoxins (STs) and heat-labile enterotoxins in Hungary; (2) The Phadebact test was not reliable; (3) The Oxoid VET test was the most rapid and reliable test for screening of ETEC strains in Hungary.
the Oxoid VET RPLA test is a rapid, sensitive and specific method for detection of heat-stable and heat-labile enterotoxin in ETEC strains.
the Oxoid VET RPLA is a rapid, sensitive, easy and specific test for the detection of ETEC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple but reliable test for detecting ETEC.
the detection of ETEC strains in human and animal infections and the epidemiological significance of these strains.
the detection of ETEC and the epidemiology of enterotoxin-producing E. coli in Hungary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Oxoid VETRPLA test was the most suitable test for detection of LT- and ST-producers in Hungary.
the Phadebakt ETEC LT test is not reliable and should not be used.
, although ETEC are not a major pathogen in Hungary, the prevalence of ETEC is increasing, especially in travellers returning from the Far East.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Oxoid VETRPLA test is recommended for use as a screening test and the Phadebacter ETEC-Lt test is useful for confirmation.
the Oxoid VET RPLA test is the most sensitive method for the detection of LT- and ST-producing E. coli strains.
the Oxoid VET RPLA is a good method for detection of ETEC strains in the laboratory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Oxoid test is a good choice for screening ETEC strains.
we need to continue to improve our understanding of the mechanisms of enterotoxin production in order to develop new strategies to combat enterotoxigenicity.
it is not necessary to use a large number of tests to detect ETEC.
